hypothesis: Some components are shared across languages while others are language-sensitive.
evidence: Aya and Qwen multi-seed toxic-versus-detox probes; Qwen layer profile; seed-specific SAE candidate-feature inventories.
paper_claim: Toxic-to-detox representations are decodable and partially transferable, but shared SAE features are not yet cross-seed aligned.

hypothesis: High-resource directions transfer to Yoruba/isiXhosa less strongly than within-language directions.
evidence: HR-to-LR probe AUC; English-to-Yoruba/isiXhosa exploratory steering copy-rate comparisons; stored per-language vectors.
paper_claim: Representational transfer is weaker on yo/xh; steering changes low-resource outputs, but archived intervention metrics do not validate detoxification benefit.

hypothesis: Activation steering can improve detoxification while preserving content, with an over-steering trade-off.
evidence: mT5 Amharic strength sweep; MT0 strength sweep; Aya verified zero-strength null control; Qwen steering exclusion audit.
paper_claim: Steering produces strength-dependent output changes without mode collapse in the recovered Amharic sweep; validated non-toxicity improvement requires clean paired confirmation.

hypothesis: Human ratings should validate non-toxicity, meaning, fluency, and acceptability.
evidence: Protocol and 500 sampled outputs exist; completed labels and agreement statistics are absent.
paper_claim: Do not use human evaluation as outcome evidence; report only protocol readiness and planned annotation design.
